investigation.waitUntil_call_chain_confirmed: index.js fetch(): after secret+json checks, ctx.waitUntil(async()=>{ syncCommandMenu; routeMessage/routeCallbackQuery }) then returns Response('ok',200) IMMEDIATELY — the Response does NOT await the work. routeMessage->routeFreeText (gemini.js) is inside that waitUntil. Production tail evidence: a signed synthetic free-text POST produced a full log trail ('telegram sendMessage -> 400 chat not found', 'gemini dispatch failed', 'update handling failed') from inside the waitUntil-deferred block — i.e. the waitUntil work RAN TO COMPLETION in production and was NOT killed mid-flight. So 'waitUntil deferral gets silently torn down' is REFUTED for this code path.
investigation.compass_comparison_result: The contract's premise is FALSE. Compass src/index.ts stashes ctx on globalThis.__ctx then returns handleWebhook(req,env); handlers/webhook.ts processMessage work is wrapped and handed to ctx.waitUntil(work) (line ~88) — Compass DOES use waitUntil in the webhook/fetch path, structurally identical to Codex. waitUntil therefore cannot be the differentiator. Other structural differences noted: (a) Compass's outer failure handler calls safeSendError() to message the user on total failure; Codex's index.js catch only console.error's (no user-visible message). (b) Compass services/telegram.ts sendMessage returns Promise<number|null> and guards firstMsgId (never an unguarded .message_id deref). (c) Compass wrangler.toml has compatibility_flags=['nodejs_compat']; Codex has none (not implicated). (d) Compass runs GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-3.1-flash-lite; Codex runs gemini-flash-lite-latest (the model FIX_STATE v7 recorded as 503-saturated at evidence time).
other_swallowed_errors_found: index.js:40-43 outer catch does ONLY console.error('update handling failed') — no sendText to the user. Any error escaping routeMessage/routeFreeText (including the TypeError below) results in total user silence. This is the sink that produces the observed 'ack then nothing'.

telegram.js tg() returns null on ANY non-OK Telegram response (sendMessage/editMessageText). A null result is only logged, never thrown, so callers that deref result.message_id throw a TypeError OUTSIDE their try/catch.
gemini.js:359 sendText('⏳ Working on it…') is OUTSIDE the try (try begins line 360); line 361 status.message_id throws if sendText returned null.
investigation.confirmed_root_cause: PRIMARY (real-chat): Codex's conversational dispatch replies can exceed Telegram's 4096-char message cap; worker/src/telegram.js editText() passes the oversized text straight to editMessageText with NO chunking, and tg() converts the resulting 400 'message is too long' into a silent null (telegram.js:13 even suppresses the error log for editMessageText 400s). classifyAndDispatch (gemini.js:519) awaits editText(statusMessageId, reply) and never checks the null result, so the '⏳ Working on it…' placeholder is never replaced -> ack then total silence. EVIDENCE: live call to the configured model gemini-flash-lite-latest with the real function-calling dispatch payload returned a 9492-character reply (overTelegram4096=True). Compass's services/telegram.ts sendMessage chunks at 4000 chars and returns a guarded Promise<number|null>, so Compass never strands a placeholder — this is the actual behavioral difference, NOT waitUntil. SECONDARY (proven in production logs): a signed synthetic free-text POST showed sendText('⏳ Working on it…') is OUTSIDE the try (gemini.js:359), so when sendText returns null (Telegram send failure) line 361 status.message_id throws a TypeError that escapes the inner catch and lands in index.js's log-only outer catch -> silence. AGGRAVATOR: gemini-flash-lite-latest returned 503 on 3/4 live calls (model saturation, matching FIX_STATE v7's note); the swallowed-edit path turns even a retry-exhausted error message into silence. waitUntil was REFUTED as a cause: Compass uses ctx.waitUntil in the same webhook path and the production tail showed the waitUntil work running to completion.

fix.approach: Match Compass's guarantees: (1) add chunkText-based splitting (4000-char) to telegram.js and use it in sendText; make editText chunk too and RETURN whether the edit succeeded, and make tg() log editMessageText failures (stop the silent-400 suppression except 'message is not modified'); (2) classifyAndDispatch: fall back to sendText when the edit returns null so the reply is never lost; (3) routeFreeText/photo/tap-edit: null-safe status (status && status.message_id) and wrap the status send inside the try with a sendText fallback; (4) index.js outer catch: sendText the user a generic failure message (Compass safeSendError pattern) instead of log-only.

Model gemini-flash-latest -> key0 503, key1 503, key2 200, key3 200, key4 401, key5 503, key6 200. Model gemini-3.1-flash-lite (Compass's configured model) -> 200 OK on six of seven keys (only key4 401).

REAL worker geminiData() rotation loop (imported verbatim from worker/src/gemini.js) against the REAL pool: model gemini-flash-lite-latest run 1 -> all 7 keys tried, six return 503 UNAVAILABLE twice each (same-key retry), key4 returns 401, loop exhausts and THROWS err.allKeysFailed=true "all 7 Gemini key(s) failed for this request (last: Gemini 503: …high demand…)" — the exact false "all keys failed" report the operator sees. run 2 (seconds later): key0 503 then 200 OK -> SUCCESS. gemini-flash-latest: 200 OK on first key both runs.

Compass request shape (?key= query param, otherwise identical payload) on gemini-flash-lite-latest returns the identical 503 UNAVAILABLE — the auth transport (header vs query param) is NOT the differentiator.
hypothesis_tested: H1 pool read from a different KV namespace/key than the UI writes -> REFUTED: request-time read and UI read share keypool.js gemini:keys in CODEX_KV; live read returns the same 7 keys the operator sees in Settings.

H2 model/payload shape difference vs Compass (model version the keys are not provisioned for) -> CONFIRMED as the primary driver: the 503s are MODEL-side saturation ("This model is currently experiencing high demand"), not key rejection — identical on every key and on Compass's own request shape. Codex runs GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-flash-lite-latest (and gemini-flash-latest shows the same per-key 503 flakiness); Compass runs gemini-3.1-flash-lite, on which the same keys return 200. So "same keys work on Compass" because Compass asks a healthy model, not because the keys differ.

H3 keys.length race leaving an empty/partial pool -> REFUTED: pool read is a single awaited KV get; live reproduction loaded all 7 keys every run; the failure reproduced with a full 7-key pool, so it is intermittent (503-lottery), not a partial-read artifact.

H4 waitUntil-removal/timing interaction breaking KV reads -> REFUTED: geminiData receives a fully-resolved pool (getKeys awaited before the loop); reproduction shows the loop iterating all 7 keys — KV reads complete fine; the allKeysFailed throw happens AFTER the full sweep, not from an empty pool.

H5 (discovered during evidence collection) corrupted pool entry -> CONFIRMED: key[4] is a doubled-paste 106-char string that hard-fails 401 on every model; rotation absorbs it (skips to next key) but it burns one pool slot and one attempt per full sweep.
investigation.confirmed_root_cause: The "❌ Every configured Gemini API key failed" report fires when geminiData() exhausts the pool on gemini-flash-lite-latest, whose real per-attempt outcome is a saturated-model 503 UNAVAILABLE lottery (captured live: 503 on 6/7 keys x2 attempts each, then a clean 200 on the very next run seconds later). isKeyFailure() correctly classifies 503 as NOT key-specific, but the loop treats a persistent 503 the same as a dead key — rotate and count toward exhaustion — so a burst of model-side 503s across the pool collapses into the all-keys-failed error whose message falsely claims "quota exhausted or keys invalid". Two aggravators: (a) pool key [4] …yMQw is a corrupted doubled-paste (106 chars) that 401s on every model, wasting a slot; (b) Codex is pinned to the saturated gemini-flash-lite-latest alias while Compass — the operator's "keys work fine" reference — runs gemini-3.1-flash-lite, on which the identical keys return 200.

fix.approach: (1) geminiData now gives a pool whose ENTIRE round failed only on 5xx saturation (zero key-specific failures) ONE bounded whole-pool retry after a 1500ms backoff — live evidence (diag/gemini-data.mjs) showed the identical request succeeding seconds later on the same pool, so a transient model-side 503 wave no longer collapses straight into allKeysFailed. (2) The thrown allKeysFailed error now carries keyFailures/saturated tallies and a poolExhaustedByKeyFailures flag; allFailedMessage uses them to tell the truth: saturation-only pool -> "model temporarily overloaded, NOT a key problem, keys are fine, try again in a minute" instead of the false "quota exhausted or keys invalid"; genuine key failures -> accurate count of key-specific failures plus a note that any 503s seen were not key faults. (3) addKeys hygiene: the Settings -> Keys paste parser (router.js) now splits on ALL whitespace, not just newlines, so a doubled-paste with no newline (the confirmed 106-char key[4], 401 on every model) enters the pool as two valid keys instead of one permanently-dead concatenation. isKeyFailure() itself is unchanged — the fix targets the misclassification at the AGGREGATE level, exactly as confirmed by the captured evidence, not a loosening of per-attempt classification.
